summary: This regulation sets limits on how many companies a director can serve on at the same time. It includes both regular and independent roles, with specific caps for executive directors. Certain government or public-private roles are not counted towards this limit.
points: A person can act as a director in a maximum of seven listed entities.
A person can serve as an independent director in a maximum of seven listed entities.
A whole time director or managing director in any listed entity can serve as an independent director in no more than three listed entities.
The count includes both companies with listed equity shares and high value debt listed entities.
Directorships held on an ex-officio basis for public sector undertakings or public-private partnerships are excluded from the limit.
example: Mr. Sharma serves as the managing director of Stellar Tech Limited, a company with listed equity shares. He wants to help various other businesses and is invited to join multiple boards. Because he already holds a whole time managing director position, the rules state he can only serve as an independent director in a maximum of three other listed entities. Mr. Sharma carefully checks his current board positions to ensure he does not break this rule. He also notes that a special public sector board role he holds due to his official office does not count toward this total.

terms.meaning: Companies whose securities are traded on a stock exchange.
A board member who does not have a material or pecuniary relationship with the company.
A director who devotes their whole time of working hours to the company.
Holding a position automatically because of holding another office or official status.

watch: Do not forget that public sector or partnership roles held automatically by law or contract may not count toward your total directorship limit.
